key_insight: POET-X scales and sparsifies orthogonal-equivalence reparameterization so you get POET's spectrum-preserving stability with much lower memory and compute overhead — enabling efficient, stable LLM training at larger scale.
problem_solved: Original POET gives strong stability but is too memory- and compute-intensive for large LLMs; POET-X reduces that overhead while retaining spectrum preservation and training stability.
method: Scale-aware orthogonal reparameterization: replace dense orthogonal transforms with scaled, factorized representations that preserve singular-value spectra but occupy far less memory.
Efficient application: apply orthogonal-equivalence implicitly (e.g., low-rank/structured factors, block or per-channel transforms) so weight updates avoid forming full rotation matrices.
Memory/compute optimizations: combine the above with cached small factors, mixed-precision-friendly updates, and layerwise sharing to minimize runtime overhead.
impact: Makes spectrum-preserving, orthogonally reparameterized training practical for modern LLMs — lowering GPU memory and compute demands so practitioners can train larger, more stable models on the same hardware budget.
